38f83d736152635d: RIYADH, Oct 25 — Yemen’s Houthis launched wide-ranging strikes across swathes of southern Saudi Arabia on Sunday, as the kingdom announced the partial reopening of Riyadh international airport despite repeated attacks by the group.

Alerts warning of possible attacks were activated across the kingdom’s south throughout the day, with the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis saying at least 10 ballistic missiles were intercepted.
Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government fell apart.
“The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning — may God keep us safe.
“Everything is shaking because of the explosions,” one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP Sunday on condition of anonymity.
Further north, Riyadh’s international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following the Houthi strikes.
However it remained unclear to what extent the airport was operational.

The Houthi fighters have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
The group has also targeted oil infrastructure and other sites.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that Riyadh airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target”.

“The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines – as well as staff and travellers – against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said.
“The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.”
Attack warning

As the airport prepared to open, AFP journalists in Riyadh heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a “hostile aerial threat” urging them to stay in a safe place.
The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards the capital, as well as two drones in the capital area.
“Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh,” the coalition posted on X.
Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom’s southern city of Khamis Mushait.
Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city along with areas in Taif, Namas and Jazan.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that – in the space of 24 hours – they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.
The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.
The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a “huge lie”.
The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.
The flare-up in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.

The Houthi attacks have dealt a blow to Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest exporter of crude, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents, and rattling its drive to shift its international image. — AFP
fe4142110a2ac026: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) has accepted Pakatan Harapan's (PH) seat allocation for the Melaka election, despite being allocated five seats compared with nine in the 2021 election.
Its vice-president, Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, said the decision followed thorough negotiations at the coalition's highest level.
"What matters to Amanah in any election is that we have been part of PH since its formation in 2015. We have always acted, organised and carried out our campaigns as a united coalition.
"The decision by PH's top leadership was made after thorough discussions and negotiations," he said after officiating at the 2026 National Mental Health Month celebration here today.
Dzulkefly, who is also Health Minister, said all party machinery, from top leaders and middle management to the grassroots, would comply with the coalition committee's decision.
"We are grateful to have been allocated five seats, and we hope to win all of them.
"There is no benefit in being allocated many seats if we fail to win them.
"Therefore, we will do our best to support one another to ensure all PH partner candidates contesting the election win," he said.
Under the seat allocation for the Melaka election on Nov 14, PKR will contest nine state seats, DAP seven and Amanah five, bringing the coalition's total to 21 seats.

5d693c1641b79ea5: CHUKAI, Oct 25 — A Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi) staff member died after being stung by a swarm of bees while collecting honey at the agency’s farm in Ayer Putih near here yesterday.

Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the incident occurred at 9.50am when the victim, Hafizul Mat, 40, a general worker, was at MARDI’s Kemaman branch at Kilometer 18 of Jalan Ayer Putih with a colleague.
“The victim’s 44-year-old colleague had advised him against collecting the honey because the beehive was on a dry tree about three metres tall, but the victim insisted on proceeding.
“The victim asked his colleague to wait about 50 metres from the beehive before climbing the tree to collect the honey, but he was attacked by a swarm of bees,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Razi said that while in the tree, the victim shouted at his colleague to run as the bees swarmed him. He then climbed down and jumped into a nearby pool of water to avoid being stung.
Mohd Razi said the victim later complained of pain in his arms and legs from the stings before getting out of the pool and collapsing unconscious with convulsions.
“The victim’s colleague then sought help from two other co-workers before calling an ambulance. The victim was taken to Kemaman Hospital for further treatment,” he said.
However, Mohd Razi said the hospital confirmed that the victim died while receiving treatment at 6.42pm. — Bernama
ea5089422f5ee693: TOKYO: Former world number one Naomi Osaka cast doubt on her future Sunday saying she would consider quitting tennis if her three-year-old daughter asked her to.
The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan took 15 months away from the sport after the birth of her daughter Shai, before returning in 2023.
She is in Tokyo to play at the Pan Pacific Open this week and said becoming a mother had reshaped her priorities.
"I wouldn't say I'm part-timing it but my entire day doesn't consist of that," said the 29-year-old, now ranked 19 in the world.
"It's tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I'm going to play.
"Because if my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that."
Osaka also stepped away from tennis in 2021 to prioritise her mental health.
She said her "mindset is changing a lot" with age.
"My daughter is my biggest priority," she said.
"I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis.
"If I think about it in certain ways, I'm really proud of where I am now because it's not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport."
- Online abuse -
Osaka said juggling her duties as a player and a mother was something she was "figuring out little by little."
She also offered support to the American Coco Gauff, who said she had received an "insane" amount of racist abuse on the internet at this month's China Open.
World number five Gauff, who is Black, said the experience had been "kind of draining."
Osaka, whose mother is Japanese and father from Haiti, said "nobody should have to go through that."
"It's sad but I'm used to it on my end," she said.
"I feel like for me, I've dealt with that my entire career through decisions that I make that seem to make some people upset. It's tough."
Osaka said efforts made by women's tennis governing body the WTA to combat social media abuse did not "ever seem to fully work all the way."
"I know that some people are like, OK, if it bothers you that much, stay off social media," said Osaka.
"But sometimes that's the best way to connect with your fans.
"From my end, what I do about it is I don't really go on social media at all."
Osaka is seeded seven in Tokyo and plays Italy's Jasmine Paolini in the first round.
World number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala are also competing.
Osaka said she was "not far off" refinding her best form and was "optimistic for next year."

0e5c031ac041f9b5: NINGBO (China), Oct 25 — World number one Elena Rybakina won her fourth title of an outstanding season with a ruthless straight-sets victory over Leylah Fernandez in the Ningbo Open final on Sunday.
The top seed and defending champion cruised to a 6-2, 6-2 win over the world number 30 from Canada.
Rybakina, the Australian and US Open champion, collected her 15th WTA crown in all and went a long way towards securing the year-end number-one ranking.
Rybakina broke and then held her own serve with a delicious two-handed crosscourt backhand for a 4-2 lead in the opening set.
The Moscow-born Kazakh immediately put Fernandez under pressure again on the Canadian’s serve and it was soon 5-2 to the reigning champion when her opponent fired into the net.
The 27-year-old Rybakina, who missed this month’s Wuhan Open with a foot injury, began to turn the screw and sealed the set to love in under 40 minutes.
Fernandez, who was looking to win her second title in as many months, was broken once more as a clinical Rybakina grabbed a 2-1 second-set lead.
Rybakina saw off two break points in the fourth game to hold, and with that, Fernandez’s resistance was broken.
Rybakina was within sight of retaining her trophy after breaking once more for 5-2, then sealed the deal on her first championship point with a searing forehand. — AFP

92140713790dcae1: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is finalising a workplace mental health policy.
This is after more than 55,000 civil servants were found to be at high risk of mental health issues, including suicidal tendencies.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said engagement sessions with stakeholders were ongoing, and an official announcement would be made once the policy was finalised.

"We are still in the process of broader stakeholder consultations. We want to avoid creating a policy in silo, or developed without sufficient cross-agency input," he told reporters after the 2026 National Mental Health Month Celebration today.

In his speech earlier, Dzulkefly cited a Public Service Department report based on its MyPsyD screening system, which found more than 55,000 civil servants to be at high risk of mental health issues, including suicidal tendencies.
"These findings serve as a timely reminder that the workplace is not merely a platform for pursuing key performance indicators (KPIs) and productivity," he said.
He said depression among adults had doubled from 500,000 in 2019 to one million in 2023, according to the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS).
"We are also witnessing emotional distress and suicidal behaviour taking a toll on our younger generation," he said.
He added that more engagements were required to complete the mental health policy draft, and an official announcement would be made once it has been finalised.

In July, Dzulkefly had said the engagement sessions would involve the Human Resources Ministry, Occupational Safety and Health Department, Malaysian Employers Federation and Malaysian Trades Union Congress.
0aa217e20d28357c: TOKYO, Oct 25 — Japanese athlete Masatora Kawano set a men’s marathon race walk world record at the All Japan Race Walking meeting in Yamagata Prefecture on Sunday, finishing the 42.195-kilometre course in 2 hours, 55 minutes and 14 seconds, Kyodo News reported.
World Athletics approved the marathon race walk, contested over the traditional marathon distance, as the replacement for the 35-km race walk at major championships in December 2024.
It officially introduced the new event in January this year and set 2:56:30 as the performance standard required for the inaugural men’s world record, with Kawano the first to break that barrier.
The meet in the town of Takahata served as a qualifier for the World Athletics Championships in Beijing next September.
Australia’s Rebecca Henderson also set a world record in winning the women’s race with a time of 3:14:52.
Kawano, 28, is a two-time world championships medalist and former world record holder in the 35-km event.
He finished sixth in the men’s 50-km race at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. — Bernama-Kyodo
4101b355b62be697: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Labuan and six states until 9pm tonight.

In Sabah, the affected areas are the Interior, West Coast and Kudat divisions, as well as Paitan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan and Tongod in the Sandakan division, and Kalabakan in the Tawau division. — Bernama
b16d7fb4c865959e: KUALA LUMPUR: South Korean singer-actor Lee Junho has fallen head over heels for Malaysia's local dishes, revealing that nasi lemak and roti tisu topped his list of favourite treats during his visit here.
The 36-year-old star shared his delight at trying authentic local food, noting that the roti tisu stood out in particular due to its towering height and impressive size.
The Typhoon Family actor described sampling the crispy, paper-thin flatbread with a variety of dips as a uniquely fun experience.
"Yesterday, I had the chance to try nasi lemak and roti tisu. Both were extremely delicious. I am not sure why it is called roti tisu, but its towering height and sheer size really caught my eye.

"I had so much fun tearing it apart piece by piece starting from the top. It was quite a fascinating experience because I got to pair it with various sauces and toppings," he said during an exclusive media session held at TGV Cinemas, Pavilion Bukit Jalil, here today.
Junho added that he sampled the roti tisu alongside several dip choices, including curry, chocolate, and pistachio.
"I love pistachio, so I tried it with that. I also had it with condensed milk, and everything tasted amazing," he shared.
Beyond his food adventures, Junho expressed his heartfelt gratitude for the chance to perform for his Malaysian fans at the Cuckootopia concert, held at Stadium Merdeka yesterday.
He noted that the event marked a fresh milestone in his career.
It was his first time joining the Cuckootopia lineup, giving him a chance to reconnect with fans he had not seen in a long while.
"This was my first time taking part in the Cuckootopia concert, so it was a very enjoyable experience for me.
"I was so happy to see the fans yesterday. If given the opportunity to attend another concert like this in the future, I would be absolutely thrilled," he added.
Organised to celebrate Cuckoo's 12th Anniversary, and as a follow-up to Anugerah Melodi Terhangat (AMT) 2026, the Cuckootopia concert ran from 6pm until midnight.
The event featured Junho in his role as Cuckoo's Global Brand Ambassador, performing alongside local music icons including Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza, rock outfit Hujan, and singer Firdhaus.
On his acting career, Junho also reflected on his participation in the second season of the reality show Kian's Bizarre B&B, describing the project as an exciting new challenge in his journey.

954533f35a484301: SINGAPORE, Oct 25 — A former healthcare worker came to the aid of a cabin crew member who required medical attention on a Singapore Airlines flight on Oct 17.
The incident occurred at about 7pm onboard SQ843 from Chengdu, China, to Singapore, according to Shin Min Daily News.
In a Xiaohongshu post on Wednesday (Oct 21), user Nicole K shared that announcement was made asking for assistance from medical personnel onboard the flight not long after takeoff.
The plane had earlier departed from Chengdu Tianfu International Airport at around 6.32pm, according to flight tracking website FlightAware.
The woman wrote how she was hesitant about stepping forward as she assumed there must be other doctors onboard the flight.
She added that she was also scared since she had not worked in an emergency room (ER) for a long time.
When a second announcement was made, she reconsidered and stepped in to offer assistance.
She saw a young cabin crew member lying weakly on the floor and went over to check his pulse.
The woman said that she could feel his pulse, although it was very weak.
She also noted that his hands and feet felt cold.
The groggy man could barely speak and answer her properly, only saying that he felt nauseous.
Grateful her years in the ER were put to use
The woman requested for a stethoscope from the cabin crew and asked for their assistance to check the man’s blood pressure, oxygen levels and blood sugar before she could reassess him.
She assessed that he required an intravenous, or IV, drip for medicine.
“His veins are hard to find, let me try first,” she said to the cabin crew, telling them to prepare extra catheters on standby.
The woman established an IV line on her first attempt, adding that she was grateful that all her years working in the ER had not gone to waste.
She then administered anti-nausea medication to him and continued to monitor his condition.
After 30 minutes, she observed that the man’s condition had stabilised with a stronger pulse and lower heart rate.
She noted that it was only 8.30pm and that they were expected to land in three hours.
The woman then decided to stay by the ill man’s side, observing him until they landed.
She said she only breathed a sigh of relief after handing him over to the medical team on the ground.
“Huge thanks to the Singapore Airlines crew for this rescue mission,” wrote the woman.
“Without a familiar medical team on the plane, everything had to be communicated step-by-step, but they were super cooperative — helping [to] find equipment and caring for the patient.”
She admitted that she was also proud of herself for stepping up, even though she was nervous.
The post has amassed over 12,000 likes on Xiahongshu, with 550 comments commending the woman for her courage.
One passenger also commented that she was onboard the flight when she heard the announcement and realised there was an emergency.

“Seeing you step forward was incredibly reassuring ... Knowing there was professional medical personnel onboard made me feel much more at ease. Thank you so much for your courage and kindness,” commented the passenger. — AsiaOne
aac8c615a69c46dd: YAN: Residents of Kampung Titi Teras and Kampung Teroi Bukit at the foot of Gunung Jerai are facing floods again after five hours of continuous heavy rain caused a river to overflow into their homes early today.
Kampung Titi Teras Village Community Council chairman Kamarudin Arifin said initial checks found about 20 houses affected by the floods.
He said residents grew worried and prepared for possible flooding whenever heavy rain continued.
"Since the beginning of the year, the area has been flooded more than five times, with the latest incident on Sept 20.
"Some residents have moved out, while others have remained in their homes. I hope they will be prepared if the weather gets worse," he said when met here today.
Kampung Titi Teras resident Sharip Saod, 75, said heavy rain that began at about 10pm yesterday caused water levels to rise at around 3am.
He said he, his wife and their son, who is in his 40s, stayed awake to monitor the water level and ensure their family's safety.
"We have been awake since last night because the rain has not stopped. So far, things are still under control. We have moved whatever household belongings we could save to the side.
"It is exhausting to be hit by floods so often, but there is nothing we can do except face it," he said.
Yan Civil Defence Force officer Lieutenant (PA) Muhammad Zul Izzi Zulkifli advised residents, particularly the elderly and other vulnerable groups, to evacuate if instructed by the authorities.
Monitoring showed that water levels had yet to change significantly and could rise further due to the high tide, delaying the recession of floodwaters, he said.
He said the Malaysian Meteorological Department had also forecast continuous rain in the area over the next few days.

The latest data showed that 105 flood victims in two districts had been affected. Of these, 65 were housed at the SK Teroi temporary relief centre in Yan, while another 40 were at the Surau As Saadiah relief centre in Gurun, Kuala Muda.
ff09fe1ab1579d9e: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) must continue to lead the state government to ensure the continuity of socioeconomic development and to keep the future of the people on the right track, said Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan.

He urged the people of Sarawak to support GPS in the 13th state election, noting that the current administration has demonstrated a clear direction in driving inclusive progress that encompasses both urban and rural areas.

"That is why we have no other choice. Our choice is the existing government led by the Premier of Sarawak (Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg), the GPS government which has a clear vision to implement transformation and elevate the well-being of the people.

"We (GPS) have an inclusive policy, we develop Sarawak through the cooperation of all races within the state," he said while speaking at the launching of Anjung Usahawan (Entrepreneurs' Hub) and the Sematan Industrial Park in Lundu.

Awang Tengah, who is also the Bukit Sari assemblyman, gave his assurance that GPS remains committed to strengthening the state's development agenda for the benefit of the people and future generations.
Regarding the polling date for the state election, he said the matter falls entirely under the jurisdiction of the Election Commission (EC).
"But one thing is certain, we must work together and work hard, we cannot take anything for granted. It is a matter of our collective strength and our future standing.
"We want to bequeath to our children and grandchildren a Sarawak that is more prosperous and united," he said.
Last Friday, during a special press conference, Abang Johari announced the dissolution of the Sarawak state legislative assembly, effective tomorrow, to pave the way for the 13th state election.

443989682ada6dd0: PETALING JAYA: Two MCA leaders have told DAP not to interfere in Barisan Nasional’s efforts to resolve a dispute over seat allocation for the Nov 14 Melaka election.
MCA secretary-general Chong Sin Woon said BN had its ways to resolve the matter, while MCA Youth deputy chief Mike Chong said the party does not need DAP to help determine its political direction.
Sin Woon said DAP should focus on resolving internal issues within Pakatan Harapan, particularly opposition towards a possible pact with Bersatu in Melaka.
“DAP should not stir trouble in this matter. Instead, it should focus on its internal issues, particularly the war of words among PH leaders.
“DAP leaders in Melaka have firmly said there would be no cooperation with Bersatu, but what is happening now is embarrassing for them," he told FMT.
Yesterday, PH announced only 21 candidates for the Melaka polls, even though 28 seats are up for grabs, further fuelling speculation of an alliance with Bersatu, a former component partner.
BN has announced a similar arrangement, with the Umno-led coalition contesting 21 seats while allocating seven for Perikatan Nasional.
MCA leaders protested against the BN announcement by staging a walkout at the event last night for not being consulted on the seats allocated to PN.
This drew taunts from two DAP leaders who challenged MCA to leave BN or contest the Melaka election under its own logo, including against PN.
Mike also touched on the speculation of a PH pact with Bersatu, which played a central role in the collapse of the PH-led federal government in 2020.
He asked whether DAP would be prepared to leave PH and contest under its own logo if a political cooperation with Bersatu materialises.

“DAP is busy challenging MCA to leave BN or contest under its own logo. But would DAP take similar action if PH made way for other parties, including Bersatu, which its leaders had previously opposed?
“Do not be so eager to comment on the internal affairs of others when your own internal disagreements remain unresolved,” he said.
Mike maintained that the MCA leadership sent a strong message by staging the walkout, but said differences in BN would be resolved through internal mechanisms and in the spirit of unity.
He nonetheless warned Umno that BN's spirit of cooperation would be undermined if decisions involving component parties were made without mutual agreement.
“MCA has its own political principles and convictions. The spirit of BN that has been built over the years will be tarnished if this matter is allowed to go unaddressed,” he said.

d9365e1ad067e137: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry aims to have one psychiatrist for every 40,000 people, compared with the current ratio of one for every 69,000.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the target, aimed at meeting growing demand for mental health services, would be achieved by expanding specialist training.
He said the ministry employed about 400 of the country's roughly 700 registered psychiatrists, with the rest working in the private sector.

To ease the shortage, Dzulkefly said the ministry was also adopting 'task-shifting', whereby counsellors and family medicine specialists (FMS) take on part of the mental health caseload.

d25238dfce0ba079: MADRID: Police made 128 arrests overnight in Barcelona for acts of "vandalism", damage to public property" and "looting", the regional Catalan police said on Sunday.

Footage on social media showed groups of young people, many clad in all-black, attacking businesses in Barcelona after gathering in the city centre for a rally that had not been declared to the authorities.

37403d17786a2234: KUANTAN, Oct 25 — No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries Director-General Datuk Adnan Hussain.
However, this situation cannot be interpreted as proof that the species is no longer present in the dam, following previous reports confirming the discovery of piranhas in the area.
He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species.

“No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program. However, monitoring and scientific assessment must continue to identify the presence and distribution of the species,” he said via a media statement today.
Previously, a video went viral on social media regarding the discovery of a fish allegedly resembling a piranha at the Klau Dam, Raub, sparking various reactions from the public.

The Department of Fisheries (DOF) added in the same release that, apart from catching activities, research using the environmental DNA (eDNA) method was also carried out during this programme to help detect the possible presence of piranhas in the Klau Dam.
This method allows water samples to be analysed to detect genetic material that may have been left behind by aquatic organisms.

“The final results of the eDNA research will be determined after the analysis and scientific evaluation process is completed. Therefore, any conclusion regarding the status of piranha presence in the Klau Dam must take into account these analysis results alongside relevant monitoring information and field evidence,” according to the statement.

The DOF informed that this programme also aims to reduce the alien fish population, assess the fish composition in the dam’s waters, and increase public awareness of the threat posed by alien species to aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem balance.
The programme, conducted at the approximately 25-square-kilometer dam, involved 150 participants, consisting of 100 anglers, 32 cast-net participants, and 18 gill-net participants.

“Throughout the programme, a total of 156.6 kilograms of alien fish were recorded, involving three main groups, namely Peacock Bass, Zebra Tilapia, and Javanese Carp (Lampam Jawa),” according to the statement. — Bernama

cf7dae3c81ea803e: Building a UK datacenter spans three government departments: one handles datacenter policy, another telecoms, and a third energy.
MPs this week explored what Prime Minister Andy Burnham's summer reshuffle means for businesses navigating Whitehall.

Liz Lloyd, parliamentary under-secretary of state, sits across two departments with a portfolio of responsibilities as long as a weekly shopping list. She explained to MPs this week that, following the decision to get rid of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT), liaison with the tech industry on datacenter construction fell to the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST).
Lloyd, who works across BIST and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), went on to explain that digital infrastructure sits within DCMS.
Speaking to the House of Commons Science and Technology Committee, Lloyd acknowledged that some departmental responsibilities overlapped.

"In terms of sector responsibilities, that is clear that technology, sorry, that telecom sits with DCMS and datacenters with BIST. When you're actually in an industry or you're trying to run a business, that that that is clear," the junior minister said.

Any business trying to build a datacenter might also want to know how to get power to it. As far as The Register can figure out, that would be the Department for Energy and Net Zero. Planning permission rests with local government, although the overall policy lies with the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. It may be clear, but it is hardly simple.
The problem is real, though. Earlier this month, Microsoft pulled out of plans for Britain's largest AI supercomputer because of difficulties securing power for the facility.
Elsewhere in the hearing, Lloyd was asked about the government's early 2025 claim that modernizing aging technology and digitizing processes could deliver £45 billion in productivity savings.

Asked if the government stood by the figure, the junior minister said: "The £45 billion figure was an estimate of long-term productivity gains. It wasn't a kind of one-off figure for savings… it was never a figure that was a target or a cashable savings figure."

When the figure was publicized under the Starmer government in January 2025, the press release was headed "Archaic tech sees public sector miss £45 billion annual savings." It continued: "Taxpayer funded services from the NHS to local councils are missing out on £45 billion in productivity savings because they are too often dependent on old and outdated technology."
It claimed the government would "tackle these issues" using "digital tools, AI and common sense to overhaul public sector technology." ®

522698f8258166e3: KUALA LUMPUR: Mr DIY Group (M) Bhd's exposure to rising e-commerce competition such as China's Pinduoduo free shipping campaign is among the reasons that the stock has been underperforming, according to CGS International.
The firm also attributed the slowdown to lower foreign shareholding following its reclassification to the MSCI Malaysia Small Cap Index in May.

"While the market views Mr DIY as highly exposed to rising e-commerce competition, we believe Pinduoduo's appeal is largely confined to price-sensitive purchases where immediate product availability is less important," it said in a note.
Mr DIY's stock has dropped 24.84 per cent on a year-to-date basis and 33.14 per cent over the past 12 months.
CGS International said that Pinduoduo's free shipping is a short-term marketing subsidy funded by PDD Holdings, similar to its strategy in the US and Europe.
It estimated Pinduoduo's Malaysia e-commerce market share at between RM1 billion and RM3 billion per annum or 1.4 to 3.4 per cent, less than 0.4 per cent of Malaysia's total retail sales.
As Pinduoduo does not disclose country-level gross merchandise value, the firm derived its estimates using four public data points.

Given that Pinduoduo's Malaysian push only gained traction in between March and April 2026, it is assumed that Pinduoduo's taxable low-value goods imports will grow in a similar trend as last year and the platform captures between 20 per cent and 50 per cent of the RM5.8 billion increase, implying a gross merchandise value of between RM1.2 billion and RM2.89 billion for 2026.

"Based on our assumptions, Pinduoduo likely loses between RM1.53 and RM8.22 per item shipped to Malaysia and would require an average item value of between RM49 and RM163 to break even under our low- and base-case scenarios," it said in a note.

The firm noted that Mr DIY's second-quarter operations overlapped with Pinduoduo's viral period between March and April this year but Mr DIY's transactions rose 7.3 per cent year-on-year, with gross margin held at 47.4 per cent.
"In our view, stabilising transactions per store and basket value after the price lock expiry would ease investor concerns over Pinduoduo."
The firm added that the Malaysian government's potential introduction of the E-Commerce Bill in the next parliamentary session could benefit Mr DIY and other value retailers.

CGS International cut its core net profit forecasts for Mr DIY by 8.2 per cent in the financial years 2027 (FY27) and FY28. It expects Pinduoduo's free shipping campaign to weigh on transactions and basket size in the first half of 2027 (1H27), before the proposed E-Commerce Bill takes effect in 2H27.
This reduces its FY27 and FY28 revenue forecasts by 2.6 per cent each as the firm assumes no catch-up in lost sales once free shipping normalises.
CGS International kept its "Add" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM1.90.

c9c951d79adc734c: PALANGKARAYA: Indonesian conservation workers rescued an orangutan ensnared in rope and her baby on the island of Borneo where the critically endangered animals are at risk from boar traps and wildfires, an official said Sunday.

The female orangutan named Gadis, about 25 years old, and her son Garis, 10 months, were found snared in a suspected trap early Friday near a village in Central Kalimantan province on the Indonesian part of Borneo.

"Gadis was found with the ropes tied to her upper right arm and lower left arms, and the wounds were bad because the ropes had torn deep into her flesh," local conservation official Muriansyah told AFP by telephone on Sunday.
"It looked like the ropes were set up as a wild boar snare trap," added Muriansyah, who like many Indonesians has one name.
Both were receiving treatment at the Orangutan Foundation International clinic near the village of Pangkalan Bun .
Wild boar hunting using rope snares is legal and common in parts of Indonesia as a pest control measure to protect crops, but illegal inside protected forests or national parks.
Officials have repeatedly cautioned that careless placement of snares near wildlife areas could instead trap endangered sun bears or orangutans.
Dozens of orangutans have also been rescued in recent weeks from rampant wildfires burning across Indonesia that have cloaked the Southeast Asian region in a toxic haze.
Two more were released in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Saturday after being rescued from an oil palm plantation.
Orangutans are critically endangered and only about 120,000 remain in the wild in Borneo and Sumatra - about half the number from a century ago, according to conservation group WWF.
Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature said fires were burning in habitats containing 52% of Borneo's orangutan population.

6034e6d56e014d74: KUCHING: The risk of Malaysian women developing breast cancer has risen to one in 23, compared with one in 27 previously, says Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri.
She said that based on the Malaysian National Cancer Registry Report for 2012–2016 and 2017–2021, breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women in the country.

"More concerning, the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023 found that 71 per cent of women aged 40 and above have never undergone a mammogram, while 46 per cent do not practise breast self-examination.

"This low screening rate complicates early detection efforts, even though the survival rate for patients detected at an early stage can reach 95 per cent," she said at the Sarawak state-level Breast Cancer Awareness Month event today.

Nancy said that to widen access to early breast cancer screening, the government, through the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), has introduced the Mammogram Examination Subsidy Programme since 2007.
She said the programme was later strengthened and rebranded to WeCaRe, which encompasses awareness of breast and cervical cancer among women.
As of Sept 30, she said, 598,919 women in Malaysia have benefited from the programme, including 90,075 women in Sarawak, with 88 of them testing positive for cancer.

c18c37d48dc04273: TOKYO: Former world number one Naomi Osaka cast doubt on her future Sunday saying she would consider quitting tennis if her three-year-old daughter asked her to.
The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan took 15 months away from the sport after the birth of her daughter Shai, before returning in 2023.
She is in Tokyo to play at the Pan Pacific Open this week and said becoming a mother had reshaped her priorities.
"I wouldn't say I'm part-timing it but my entire day doesn't consist of that," said the 29-year-old, now ranked 19 in the world.
"It's tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I'm going to play.
"Because if my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that."
Osaka also stepped away from tennis in 2021 to prioritise her mental health.
She said her "mindset is changing a lot" with age.
"My daughter is my biggest priority," she said.
"I try my best to put as much energy as I can into tennis.
"If I think about it in certain ways, I'm really proud of where I am now because it's not like I can dedicate my entire time to the sport," she added.
Online abuse
Osaka said juggling her duties as a player and a mother was something she was "figuring out little by little".
She also offered support to the American Coco Gauff, who said she had received an "insane" amount of racist abuse on the internet at this month's China Open.
World number five Gauff, who is Black, said the experience had been "kind of draining".
Osaka, whose mother is Japanese and father from Haiti, said "nobody should have to go through that".
"It's sad but I'm used to it on my end," she said.
"I feel like for me, I've dealt with that my entire career through decisions that I make that seem to make some people upset. It's tough," she said.
Osaka said efforts made by women's tennis governing body the WTA to combat social media abuse did not "ever seem to fully work all the way".
"I know that some people are like, OK, if it bothers you that much, stay off social media," said Osaka.
"But sometimes that's the best way to connect with your fans.
"From my end, what I do about it is I don't really go on social media at all," she said.
Osaka is seeded seven in Tokyo and plays Italy's Jasmine Paolini in the first round.
World number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and Philippines sensation Alexandra Eala are also competing.
Osaka said she was "not far off" refinding her best form and was "optimistic for next year".

"Fasa kedua pula bermula pada Rabu dengan semua sekolah di seluruh Johor dijadual beroperasi sepenuhnya seperti biasa, tertakluk kepada perkembangan semasa kualiti udara," katanya dalam kenyataan.

Naqib berkata sehubungan dengan itu, Jabatan Pendidikan Negeri Johor akan menyelaras pelaksanaan prosedur operasi standard kesihatan dan keselamatan termasuk pemakaian pelitup muka serta pemantauan aktiviti persekolahan, berdasarkan bacaan Indeks Pencemar Udara (IPU) semasa.

Beliau berkata pada masa sama, kerajaan negeri bersama dengan agensi berkaitan akan terus memantau perkembangan situasi jerebu secara berterusan bagi memastikan sebarang tindakan dapat dilaksana berdasarkan penilaian keadaan semasa.
Semalam, Kerajaan Negeri Johor memutuskan semua institusi pendidikan akan kembali beroperasi esok setelah mengambil kira perkembangan situasi jerebu dan penilaian agensi berkaitan.
Hanya dua daerah di Johor mencatatkan IPU tidak sihat, iaitu Pasir Gudang dengan bacaan 154 dan Batu Pahat (127) setakat 4 petang tadi.
664c43e4288eb328: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 25 — Schools in Johor will reopen in phases, with the first phase on Monday (tomorrow) and Tuesday limited to students sitting for examinations according to the scheduled timetable.

State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made following the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, who places great importance on the safety, health and well-being of the people of Johor.
He said the arrangement would also give school administrators and teachers time to prepare for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) and Ujian Akhir Sesi Akademik (UASA) examinations.
“The second phase will begin on Wednesday, when all schools throughout Johor are scheduled to resume full operations as usual, subject to developments in air quality,” he said in a statement today.

Muhammad Naqib said the Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) would coordinate the implementation of health and safety standard operating procedures (SOPs), including the wearing of face masks and monitoring of school activities, based on current air pollutant index (API) readings.

He said the state government and relevant agencies would continue to monitor the haze situation closely to ensure that any necessary action could be taken based on assessments of prevailing conditions.

Yesterday, the Johor state government decided that all educational institutions would resume operations tomorrow after taking into account developments in the haze situation and assessments by the relevant agencies.
As of 4 pm today, only two districts in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pasir Gudang at 154 and Batu Pahat at 127. — Bernama

a7869eb2219d9951: KUANTAN: No piranha fish were found or caught during the Alien Fish Mitigation Programme at the Klau Dam, Raub, which took place over two days starting yesterday, said Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain.
However, this situation cannot be interpreted as proof that the species is no longer present in the dam, following previous reports confirming the discovery of piranhas in the area.
He said this mitigation program is one of the inland fisheries management efforts to control alien fish populations and reduce the risk of disruption to native fish species.

"No piranha fish were found or caught throughout this program. However, monitoring and scientific assessment must continue to identify the presence and distribution of the species," he said via a media statement today.
Previously, a video went viral on social media regarding the discovery of a fish allegedly resembling a piranha at the Klau Dam, Raub, sparking various reactions from the public.

The Fisheries Department added in the same release that, apart from catching activities, research using the environmental DNA (eDNA) method was also carried out during this programme to help detect the possible presence of piranhas in the Klau Dam.
This method allows water samples to be analysed to detect genetic material that may have been left behind by aquatic organisms.

"The final results of the eDNA research will be determined after the analysis and scientific evaluation process is completed. Therefore, any conclusion regarding the status of piranha presence in the Klau Dam must take into account these analysis results alongside relevant monitoring information and field evidence," according to the statement.

The department said that this programme also aims to reduce the alien fish population, assess the fish composition in the dam's waters, and increase public awareness of the threat posed by alien species to aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem balance.
The programme, conducted at the approximately 25sqkm dam, involved 150 participants, consisting of 100 anglers, 32 cast-net participants, and 18 gill-net participants.

"Throughout the programme, a total of 156.6kg of alien fish were recorded, involving three main groups, namely Peacock Bass, Zebra Tilapia, and Javanese Carp (Lampam Jawa)," according to the statement.
c23f09f142b73970: PETALING JAYA: Pucuk pimpinan Bersatu akan memuktamadkan jumlah kerusi yang bakal ditandingi parti itu pada PRN Melaka menerusi mesyuarat diadakan esok.
Ketua Penerangan Bersatu Melaka, Hishamuddin Abdul Karim, berkata keputusan itu termasuk penggunaan logo parti berkenaan.
“Esok mesyuarat MPT, keputusan akhir akan diumumkan,” katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau berkata demikian ketika diminta mengulas sama ada Bersatu akan bertanding tujuh kerusi pada PRN Melaka susulan keputusan Pakatan Harapan (PH) hanya bertanding di 21 daripada 28 kerusi DUN.
Sebelum ini, timbul khabar angin bahawa PH berkemungkinan mengadakan persefahaman pilihan raya dengan Bersatu.
Sementara itu, sumber dalam kalangan pemimpin MPT Bersatu memaklumkan parti itu hampir pasti mengadakan kerjasama dengan PH.
“Setakat ini kami hampir pasti akan bekerjasama dengan PH. Dalam PRN Melaka 14 November ini, pengumuman rasmi akan dibuat pucuk pimpinan,” katanya.
Beliau turut memaklumkan Bersatu tidak akan bertanding di semua tujuh kerusi yang ditinggalkan PH, sebaliknya kerusi berkenaan akan ditandingi parti lain.
PH sebelum ini mengumumkan akan bertanding di 21 kerusi, namun gabungan itu tidak menyatakan parti mana yang akan bertanding di baki tujuh kerusi.
Perkara itu terus menjadi tanda tanya di tengah-tengah spekulasi mengenai kerjasama dengan Bersatu.
Selain PH, BN turut mengumumkan akan bertanding di 21 kerusi, sambil memaklumkan baki tujuh kerusi akan ditandingi PAS dan rakan-rakannya.
7fcc81309dd18472: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 25 — The Johor government expects 26,000 job opportunities to be offered to young people across the state this year, driven by rapid economic growth and the influx of high-value investments.

Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the projected figure reflected a consistent year-on-year increase, following the success of various strategic initiatives, including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and large-scale career events such as the Johor Talent Development Council (JTDC) Mega Job Fair.
He said the state had continued to record a significant increase in quality job opportunities compared with previous years.
“A total of 15,000 job opportunities were offered in 2022, rising to 17,000 in 2024 and surging to 24,000 in 2025, before reaching a target of 26,000 this year,” he said.

“For comparison, the JTDC Mega Job Fair alone offered 3,000 job opportunities, 30 per cent of which, or 1,000 positions, were in the premium-salary category,” he said when delivering his speech at the closing ceremony of the JTDC Mega Job Fair at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre (TMIYC) in Iskandar Puteri here today.

Elaborating further, Onn Hafiz said Johor’s strong economic performance was also supported by a gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate of 8 per cent, the highest in the country’s history, as well as investment inflows reaching RM110 billion.

However, he said these macroeconomic growth figures must translate into tangible benefits for the people, particularly young people and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), so that they could genuinely share in the state’s prosperity.
“These figures must not simply look good on paper; the people must feel and enjoy the benefits of the development taking place in the state,” he said.

In line with efforts to strengthen human capital, he said the state government was also emphasising the importance of reskilling and upskilling programmes to ensure the local workforce met the standards required by high-paying industries in advanced manufacturing, logistics, energy and data centres. — Bernama
bd408a694fbbcb4f: \KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu has warned that today's emergency Perikatan Nasional (PN) Supreme Council meeting could carry serious legal implications as the coalition's registration has been cancelled.
Bersatu secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said all parties should preserve the status quo of the Registrar of Societies' decision until all court proceedings had been exhausted.

He questioned why Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had issued the invitation to the meeting on Oct 23 when a notice of appeal had been filed at the Court of Appeal on the same day on behalf of the Registrar of Societies and the Home Minister.

"If Pas and its allies still proceed with the 'Perikatan Nasional Supreme Council' meeting in the situation explained above, Bersatu is concerned that the proceedings of the meeting and the decisions made at it carry serious legal implications," he said in a statement today.
He said that although PN obtained a stay from the High Court on Oct 22, the court had noted that the deregistration had already taken effect.
"The court also accepted that a stay order cannot be automatically deemed to restore a registration that has been cancelled," he said.
He said that under the Societies Act 1966, a deregistered society becomes unlawful, while any office-bearer or person managing it commits an offence punishable by up to five years in jail.

"Bersatu will bring this matter to be discussed with lawyers to ensure that the implementation of the law in accordance with the PN Constitution and the Societies Act 1966 is carried out lawfully and in an orderly manner," he said.

He added that the meeting's organisers must first state their position on the Bersatu Supreme Leadership Council quorum issue and Bersatu's membership in PN. He said these issues had been used to deny the party's right to attend and vote at the coalition's Supreme Council meeting on July 16.
"They also often dispute Bersatu's membership when Bersatu is a legitimate member party of PN, as affirmed by the Registrar of Societies in a letter dated Aug 12, 2026," he said.

On Oct 13, the High Court granted PN leave to initiate a judicial review against two actions by the Registrar of Societies: a show-cause notice under Section 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966 and an order under Section 13(2)(A) suspending the coalition's activities.

The Registrar of Societies confirmed on Oct 20 that it had cancelled PN's registration, saying the coalition's explanation had failed to address the grounds for cancellation outlined in an earlier notice.

85882373d1a23530: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 25 — Police recently arrested six individuals, including four Bangladeshi men, suspected of being involved in an online gaming scam syndicate.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the syndicate, which operated from an abandoned hotel in Taman Lagenda near here, was believed to have been active since June.

“In a raid at 9.30pm on Wednesday (October 21), a team of officers and personnel from the Kuala Muda District Police Headquarters (IPD) Commercial Crime Investigation Division (CCID) arrested four Bangladeshi men aged between 20 and 53.

“The group targeted victims among the Bangladesh community. They are believed to have received salaries of about RM2,700 per month to carry out the activities,” he told a press conference at the Kuala Muda IPD here today.

Hanyan said further investigations led to the arrest of two Malaysian men aged 40 and 50 in a raid on Friday (October 23), adding that they were believed to be the premises owner and an agent who handled the process of renting the premises to the suspects.
The syndicate is believed to have handled online game credit top-ups and used a website and WhatsApp to communicate with customers.
“Customers’ withdrawals of their winnings were deliberately delayed, with the status shown as ‘pending withdrawal’, resulting in them not receiving the money.
“Based on preliminary information, about 17 customer accounts a day were believed to have encountered the problem, with estimated losses of around RM2,000 a day,” he said.
Hanyan said police seized various items, including 17 mobile phones, four computer processing units (CPUs), eight monitors, two modems, a laptop and RM2,442 in cash.
Further investigations are ongoing under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code. — Bernama

50937a197e15b8bf: TOKYO, Oct 25 — Japanese automakers are stepping up efforts to shorten their vehicle development times as they seek to catch up with Chinese rivals that offer new models to global markets more quickly and to better respond to changing customer demand, Kyodo News reported.

Toyota Motor Corp, Honda Motor Co, Nissan Motor Co and other Japanese carmakers typically spend around four to five years developing a new model, more than twice as long as the less than two years taken by Chinese companies.
As part of its reform measures, Nissan aims to slash development times under its new family-based vehicle development strategy.
The carmaker will design a common platform for multiple models of the same size.
The carmaker, for example, plans to shorten the lead time for developing a new sport-utility vehicle model to three years and one month for launch in North America in 2028.
It will then use the same platform as that of the new SUV for its derivative models, enabling it to reduce development time by up to 40 per cent to two and a half years.
The new product strategy will cover 80 per cent of the company’s global sales and is expected to cut the number of part types by 70 per cent.
“This is a reform to become a company that responds to changes and delivers good cars in a timely manner,” Hidemi Sasaki, deputy general manager of Nissan’s product planning division, said.

Honda, seeking a V-shaped recovery from its first net loss in the last fiscal year, has introduced the “Triple Half” approach designed to halve development costs, time frames and workloads from 2025 levels, making full use of artificial intelligence and other digital technologies.
The new initiatives will begin with new models whose development the company will start in 2028.
Toyota, the world’s largest automaker by volume, is also working to reduce types of parts, depending on customer needs, as fewer parts will improve productivity and speed up development work.
Naming the project “Area 35”, Toyota aims to improve the use of plant floor space by 35 per cent.

Suzuki Motor Corp. plans to halve its current development time to around two years, while Mitsubishi Motors Corp also aims to shorten the period by 20 per cent to three years by around 2030. — Bernama-Kyodo
b3a2c632cb12d7fe: RIYADH: Explosions rang out in the Saudi capital on Sunday, as the kingdom was due to reopen Riyadh international airport despite repeated attacks by Yemen's Houthis.
Saudi Arabia, which leads a military coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthis, has faced a barrage of strikes from the group in recent weeks.
The fighting erupted after a years-long truce between the Houthis and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government fell apart, and has shifted the focus of the wider US-Iran war.
Riyadh's international airport said flights would resume on Sunday after a two-week closure following the Houthi strikes.
However, it remained unclear to what extent the airport was operational.

The Houthi fighters have carried out waves of strikes on the airport, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that the facility was still "unsafe" and a "military target".

"The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines - as well as staff and travellers - against using King Khalid Airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces," he said.
"The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport," he added.
Attack warning
An AFP journalist in the city heard three explosions in the early hours of Sunday, with residents receiving alert messages for a "hostile aerial threat" urging them to stay in a safe place.
The warning came as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had downed a ballistic missile launched by the group towards Riyadh, as well as two drones in the capital area.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh," the coalition posted on X.
Later Sunday morning, the coalition said its forces intercepted a cruise missile fired by the Houthis at the kingdom's southern city of Khamis Mushait.
Attacks appeared to target areas across the south, with warnings also issued for Abha city and Namas Governorate.

"The bombardment has been very heavy since this morning - may God keep us safe. Everything is shaking because of the explosions," one resident in Khamis Mushait told AFP Sunday on condition of anonymity.
The attacks came after the Houthi fighters said that - in the space of 24 hours - they targeted three Saudi airports, including in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an air base.
The Saudi civil defence agency said it had also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.
The Houthis denied targeting the cities, the two holiest in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a "huge lie".
The Houthis also fired at the southern Yemeni city of Aden, the interim seat of the Saudi-backed government, saying they targeted a naval base and military camp overseen by Saudi forces.
The flare-up in Yemen, with the Houthis taking control of the entire Red Sea coast in a lightning offensive last month, has further destabilised the region and disrupted oil markets.
The Houthi attacks have dealt a blow to Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude, disrupting businesses, airlines and residents, and rattling its drive to shift its international image.
1c78bc3df218ef7f: KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation with Bersatu could help Pakatan Harapan (PH) reach more Malay voters in next month's Melaka election, but wresting power from Barisan Nasional (BN) will remain difficult.
Universiti Malaya senior political science lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said PH would need to win 15 of the 28 seats contested, but several factors favoured BN.
These included the performance of Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, BN's "poster boy", the performance of several BN assemblymen, and Umno-BN's popularity and grassroots strength in Melaka.

Mohammad Tawfik said DAP's four seats in Kota Laksamana, Kesidang, Bandar Hilir and Ayer Keroh would be difficult to challenge, as each had previously been won with a majority of more than 5,000 votes.

"However, it is still too early to predict what majorities DAP candidates could regain, given the possibility of a 10 per cent shift in Chinese voter sentiment, as seen in previous state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negri Sembilan.
"At the same time, I expect fierce contests in the two seats currently held by MCA, Machap Jaya and Klebang, both of which have majorities of fewer than 1,000 votes," he said when contacted today.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, PH won five seats, four through DAP and one through Amanah, while PKR failed to win any.
PH was previously reported to be considering cooperation with Bersatu for the 16th Melaka election, with PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari tasked with examining the prospects.

Neither side had made an official announcement as of today. Last night, PH announced it would contest 21 seats, with PKR fielding candidates in nine, DAP in seven and Amanah in five. The remaining seven seats were not announced and were believed to be intended for a coalition partner.
Mohammad Tawfik said experience in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections showed that political cooperation did not necessarily lead to an automatic transfer of votes, including Malay votes.
He said Bersatu's support could not be assumed to transfer directly to PH, and the party's poor performance in the previous Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections could be repeated in Melaka.

"Bersatu's support was previously 'siphoned off' by Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), a breakaway from Bersatu. In Negri Sembilan, for example, Bersatu lost all 24 seats and recovered its election deposit in only one, Jeram Padang.

"In my view, this development is alarming for Bersatu. PH needs to be cautious about this cooperation because it could drain its campaign machinery and financial resources without necessarily improving the chances of winning seats contested by Bersatu," he said.
a0c33964ded36c4f: MELAKA: PKR mempertaruhkan tujuh muka baharu daripada sembilan calon yang diketengahkan bagi menghadapi PRN Melaka bulan depan.

06178e1dbabc55cf: DARMSTADT (Germany), Oct 25 — Author Christine Wunnicke has been awarded the 2026 Georg Buchner Prize, one of the most prestigious literary honours in the country, at a ceremony in Darmstadt, in western Germany, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
“Thank you very much for the wonderful Buchner Prize.
“I’m still stunned,” Wunnicke said at the city’s State Theatre on Saturday evening.
Established in 1951, the prize carries €50,000 (US$56,000, RM229,000) in prize money.
“What I enjoy doing most when writing, and what I’m best at, is cutting,” Wunnicke said in her acceptance speech, explaining why her books had become increasingly short.
She said she had even cut her acceptance speech down to a single sentence.
In the end, however, she chose to read Buchner’s work and take the train instead.
“I often read on public transport because I can concentrate so well there,” she said, before recounting her observations of people and her surroundings.
The German Academy for Language and Literature, which awards the prize, praised Wunnicke for her consistently surprising and masterfully crafted narratives.
The jury said her work revealed fictional elements in seemingly historical settings, offering fresh perspectives on Europe’s scientific and colonial history.
The award is named after dramatist and revolutionary Georg Buchner, best known for his plays Woyzeck and Danton’s Death.
Born in 1813 in what was then the Grand Duchy of Hesse, he died in Zurich in 1837.
Two other prizes were also presented at the ceremony.
Historian of science Anke te Heesen received the Sigmund Freud Prize, while author and literary critic Helmut Bottiger won the Johann Heinrich Merck Prize.
Each carries €20,000 (RM91,700) in prize money. — Bernama-dpa

348f17b5fc42b54b: PETALING JAYA: Schools in Johor will reopen in stages following their closure because of the haze, starting with examination candidates tomorrow and on Tuesday.
Johor education and information committee chairman Dr Naqib Ghazali said the decision was made following a decree by the regent, Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim.

In Serian, Sarawak, however, 27 schools in the Tebedu district will be temporarily closed tomorrow, with the air pollutant index (API) reading at IPD Serian reaching 194 as of 5pm.
The Sarawak education department said the closure would involve one secondary school and 26 primary schools under its supervision, Bernama reported.
API readings of between zero and 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 301 and above as hazardous.
Four other areas in Sarawak also had "unhealthy" API readings, with Kuching recording 182, Samarahan 179, Sri Aman 158, and Sibu 141.
Also recording unhealthy air quality were Paka, Terengganu (156) and Pasir Gudang, Johor (153).
Fifty-two locations nationwide recorded "moderate" API readings, and nine had good air quality.
ac8ee4cfd81cb776: KEMAMAN: A man died after being stung by a swarm of bees while trying to collect honey from a tree in Batu 18, Jalan Air Putih, Terengganu yesterday.
Hafizul Mat Nor, 40, was attacked by the bees about 9.50am.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Razi Rosli said the victim had asked a 44-year-old friend to accompany him to collect the honey.
He said the friend initially told the victim not to take the honey as the tree was very tall, but the victim decided to climb it anyway.
"While climbing the tree, a swarm of bees suddenly attacked and stung the victim.
"At that point, the victim shouted for his friend to run to safety.
"The victim tried to climb back down to save himself, and both of them ran into a pool of water at a nearby plantation," he said in a statement.
Razi said the victim then complained of pain in his legs and arms from the stings before getting out of the water and collapsing.
He said the victim's friend tried to wake him but, on realising he was unconscious and convulsing, immediately called the emergency line.
"The victim's friend immediately sought ambulance assistance before the victim was rushed to Kemaman Hospital for further treatment," he said.
He said the victim was, however, pronounced dead at the hospital at 6.42pm.
178ac36f0a9ebb6f: KOTA BARU: About 12,500 ha of padi fields under the Kemubu Agricultural Development Authority (Kada) scheduled for harvesting in November and December face flood risks during the Northeast Monsoon.
Kada chairman Khalid Abdul Samad said 56 per cent of the 25,000 ha of padi cultivation areas under the agency had been harvested for the first season of 2026 as of today.

"The remaining 44 per cent includes 11,000 ha scheduled for harvesting next month and another 1,500 ha in December, mainly in the Tumpat area. These areas could be affected if flooding occurs during the period," he said.

He said Kada implemented five monsoon preparedness measures, including maintaining drainage systems, coordinating water gate operations, operating seven active drainage pumps, scheduling the second padi planting season, and relocating assets to safer areas.
Khalid said this after the launch of the 2026 Integrity Day celebration and the Kada Corruption-Free Pledge ceremony here today.

Meanwhile, Khalid said Kada considered the average deduction rate of about 23 per cent for moisture and impurities during the first 2026 harvest season to be reasonable, adding that no complaints had been received from farmers.

He said that as of Oct 18, average deduction rates varied among Area Farmers' Organisations (PPK), with PPK Jaya Peringat recording 23 per cent, followed by PPK Sri Gunong at 23.5 per cent and PPK Tanjong Puri at 24.5 per cent.
He said Kada will monitor the padi grading process and investigate any complaints about deductions deemed excessive or unreasonable.
Padi farmers were also advised to follow the established planting schedule to avoid harvesting during the monsoon season, which could affect padi quality and result in higher deduction rates.
Khalid said grading was based on the quality of padi delivered to mills, including the presence of foreign matter, empty grains, damaged or immature grains, and excessive moisture content. — BERNAMA

bd2f499d94dc6d79: KUALA LUMPUR: Mah Sing Group Bhd aims to derive 30 per cent of its group revenue from recurring income within the next five years as it diversifies its earnings base beyond property sales and expands its industrial and data centre-related opportunities.

The target represents a shift towards a more diversified earnings model, reducing reliance on property sales while building a stronger base of income from leasing commercial properties, estates and retail space.

Mah Sing founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum said recurring income, although currently contributing a relatively small share of revenue, would become an increasingly important part of the group's long-term growth strategy.

"The recurring-income ambition is part of Mah Sing's longer-term growth plans, although achieving the 30 per cent contribution will depend on expanding its income-generating portfolio and converting opportunities into sustainable revenue," he told Business Times.

Leong said the company's current priority was to grow the business and continue improving performance, with recurring income, industrial developments and land monetisation offering potential avenues to strengthen its earnings base.
Mah Sing is also exploring land sales to data centre operators and hyperscalers in Johor to capitalise on growing demand for digital infrastructure.

Its industrial property push includes MS Industrial Park @ Kulai, a RM2.2 billion joint-venture development with KLK Land Sdn Bhd spanning 419.17 acres of freehold land within Zone E of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
The partners have opened the project's sales gallery after Phase 1A recorded more than 90 per cent take-up, with Phase 1B now open for sale.

Planned across five phases, the industrial park will offer two-storey semi-detached and detached factories, industrial land parcels ranging from one to eight acres, and larger plots for customised industrial facilities and data centre developments.
Mah Sing holds a 60 per cent stake in the project, while KLK Land, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, owns the remaining 40 per cent.
Since entering Johor in 2000, Leong said the group has continued to grow its presence through residential and industrial developments.

"Our experience in developing five industrial parks across the Greater Klang Valley and Johor gives us a solid foundation as we embark on MS Industrial Park @ Kulai, our sixth industrial development. We see strong potential in Kulai, supported by the JS-SEZ, its proximity to Singapore, improving infrastructure and the continued growth of high-value industries in Johor," he said in a statement.

Meanwhile, Mah Sing plans to introduce higher-end residential products next year while maintaining its focus on homes within its established price range. Further development announcements are also expected next year.
Leong said the group's immediate priority remained growing the business and improving performance across its property segments.
Mah Sing is targeting property sales of RM2.76 billion this year after posting an eight per cent increase in net profit for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025).
Net profit rose to RM260 million from RM239.1 million a year earlier, supported by the finalisation of construction costs for projects nearing completion.
67351d0facd2f2a1: KOTA BARU: More than 1,000 people who travel daily between Kuala Besar and the islands off Tumpat face safety risks due to a badly damaged jetty they rely on to board boats.

Damaged by floods last year, the jetty has been left with broken railings and a damaged platform, raising concerns over the safety of residents and visitors travelling to islands including Pulau Suri.
Residents have resorted to placing stones beneath broken sections of the structure in an attempt to support the platform and keep the jetty usable.

Kampung Che Latiff head Wan Kamal Wan Ahmad, 61, who has served as village head for three years, said the jetty was built with federal government funding more than three years ago and had become a vital link for island communities.
He said it was used by residents, visitors and authorities, particularly during emergencies and when transporting patients to the mainland for medical treatment.
"The jetty is our main access point to the islands. It is used by residents and the authorities, including when patients need to be taken to hospital by boat before being transferred by ambulance.
"Some people have been injured after falling at the damaged jetty. We are worried that someone could suffer more serious injuries if the situation continues," he said.
Wan Kamal said residents hoped the authorities would repair or replace the structure as soon as possible.
"If possible, we hope a concrete jetty can be built to provide a safer and more durable facility for the people," said the father of three.
He said the jetty operated around the clock and served more than 60 passenger boats and 22 privately owned boats. A parking area was also available at no charge.
"The current platform is made of fibreglass, but the damaged structure remains a major concern for us," he added.
Resident Hassan Bakar, 62, said the jetty's condition was a daily concern for communities whose lives revolved around boat travel.
The father of three said thousands of people living on the islands relied on boats for their daily journeys.

Hassan said the combined population of Pulau Rejuna and Pulau Suri was about 5,000, while the wider island community had an estimated population of 10,000. However, residents of other islands use separate jetties.
Boat fares range from RM2 to RM3 per passenger, while children travel free, he said.
"The journey between the mainland and the islands takes about five to 10 minutes, making the jetty a vital link for residents travelling for work, education, medical treatment and other daily needs.
"Therefore, I believe a proper jetty is important. If necessary, a concrete jetty," he said.
9fa3730eab38f3ac: LOS ANGELES, Oct 25 — After a murder of crows kidnaps her little brother, a young girl ventures into an enchanted forest filled with talking animals and other magical beings, where a looming war will decide everyone’s fate.

This is the fanciful tale told in Wildwood, from the stop-motion animation studio Laika — an ambitious project that took 16 years to make it to the big screen, and already a frontrunner for next year’s Oscars.

“To put that in perspective, 16 years ago, Barack (Obama) was then a fresh-faced president in his very first term. Oh, it was a better time, my friends,” director Travis Knight said at the film’s premiere in Los Angeles.

“This movie exists because hundreds and hundreds of people poured years of their lives into trying to tell the most beautiful story that they could using their hands, using their imagination,” Knight explained in an interview with AFP.
“That is something that computers can’t do,” added the filmmaker, who is also the CEO of Laika, the US studio behind Coraline.

In the age of artificial intelligence, Knight extols the virtues of stop-motion, an animation technique in which the movements of tiny physical objects are captured one frame at a time, to create the effect of fluid motion when played back.
“It is a celebration of humanity because what you’re seeing in this film is human creativity, human artistry, human effort on a grand scale,” he said.
“Computers can try to emulate things that we’ve gone through, but a computer has never felt loss. It’s never felt joy. It hasn’t fallen in love. It hasn’t had its heart broken.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
‘Wildwood’ director Travis Knight attends the AFI Fest opening-night premiere of the animated feature film at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles on October 21, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Universal’

Wildwood is the story of Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) and her quest to rescue her brother, who has been taken by the crows into the Impassable Wilderness — or the forests outside Portland, Oregon, which are hidden from mere mortals.
Along with her friend Curtis (Jacob Tremblay), Prue discovers a fantastic world, but one in which ambition and grief are fuelling discord that could erupt in conflict.
“It is a big sweeping fantasy story,” Knight said.
“But it also is an exploration of mature themes and profound emotional things that everyone goes through at various times in their lives.”
Lee told AFP that Prue’s journey resonated for her, and recalled some of her own challenges in adolescence.

“I didn’t go into a magical forest,” Lee joked, but said she did understand “that idea of being a young person that feels so mature and so grown up, and feels like they have a really firm grasp on the world and reality, and then it’s sort of all put into question.”
“And all of a sudden, you have to rethink everything,” she added.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

(From left) ‘Wildwood’ director Travis Knight and voice cast Marc Evan Jackson, Awkwafina, Jacob Tremblay, Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Amandla Stenberg, Tantoo Cardinal, Jake Johnson and Angela Bassett at the AFI Fest opening-night premiere of the show at the TCL Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles on October 21, 2026. — AFP pic
Tremblay also said he could identify with Curtis, who tries to emulate the courage he sees in his favourite comic book and game characters.
The actors whose voices are featured in the film also helped shape how their characters move.
Their gestures were filmed as they recorded their lines, so that animators could incorporate those mannerisms into the movie.
Angela Bassett, Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali and Awkwafina are all part of the cast.
For its technical team, Wildwood marks a milestone in terms of the expressions created, and the menagerie of animals featured.

“Every film we’ve done has been R&D (research and development) for the next one,” said animation supervisor Brad Schiff, who explained that the subtleties in facial movement achieved were impossible just a few years ago.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
YouTube screenshot shows a scene from stop-motion animated feature’ Wildwood’ from US studio Laika, which also produced ‘Coraline’.
The film, inspired by Colin Meloy’s book of the same name, is an ode to Portland, where Laika is based.
“It is a very specific place,” said Knight, who lives in the Pacific Northwest city.
“The more specific, the more intimate you make something, ultimately the more universal it becomes.” — AFP

b901521ab5bb7e90: KUALA LUMPUR: FIFA's 12-month suspensions on Malaysia's seven naturalised footballers will end next month. So who will they play for next?
They can return to domestic leagues, but their prospects of representing Harimau Malaya are unclear.
FIFA suspended the seven players last year over falsification of their ancestral documentation in applying for heritage players status.

Four of the seven are now with Johor Darul Ta'zim. Spanish left-back Gabriel Palmero joined JDT in August after a brief stint with Kuching City, linking up with fellow FIFA-sanctioned players Joao Figueiredo, Jon Irazabal and Hector Hevel.

Argentine striker Rodrigo Holgado is set to join Bruneian outfit DPMM FC. Winger Imanol Machuca signed for Argentine club, CA Independiente, in July while centre-back Facundo Garces remains with La Liga side Deportivo Alaves.

Under Malaysian Football League (MFL) guidelines, clubs can register and field them as local players because they hold Malaysian identity cards and passports, thus exempting them from foreign-player quotas.
